resolutions: A derived action nounstem begins with the exact verb core inside an owner-issued VNC Result.
The whole finite predicate, a displayed formula, and a surface spelling cannot substitute for that core.
Copied and JSON-lookalike VNC Results cannot authorize the conversion.
Only a future VNC Result supplies the source core for these z and liz formations.
The future-tense z and the added nominal z remain different typed constituents.
A z action noun keeps final i and replaces productive final a with i.
Predictable ca to qui and hua to hui behavior follows shape rather than example identity.
A z formation outside the productive final-i or final-a environment requires a typed lexical exception.
The z action noun is a tli noun with a nonanimate common subject.
In possessive state the source VNC subject becomes the NNC possessor automatically.
Action, process, result, state, and condition readings remain contextual or lexical rather than shape-selected.
Liz is represented as l plus supportive i plus z.
Class A, B, C, and D differences arrive through the exact future core rather than a Lesson 37 class table.
Class C final-vowel loss and preceding-vowel lengthening remain visible in the inherited future core.
Class D final ā and Class A final ō remain visible in the inherited future core.
Nonspecific tē or tla and reflexive ne remain internal to the derived nounstem.
Supportive initial i deletion after tla is automatic and can be inherited from the VNC owner.
After ne, supportive initial i retention versus deletion is the one genuine boundary choice in these groups.
Changing to another valid typed Source shape while preserving clause facts preserves productive eligibility.
Groups 1 through 3 add no example-stem, manual class, manual number, copied-predicate, formula, or surface authority.
Before liz, typed final ca changes to qui and typed final ci changes to xi productively.
Typed hua and ti boundaries expose only the alternatives Canvas actually leaves open.
A frequentative destockal ca Source preserves its internal history and typed lexical selection.
An unlisted Source with the same typed boundary receives the same productive replacive rule.
Changing to an incompatible requested alternation blocks without changing the Source stem.
Root plus ya is preserved as internal morphemic structure rather than inferred from final letters.
An unlisted typed root-plus-ya Source can select licensed deletion or retention without list membership.
Denominal ti-ya deletes ya before liz from its typed boundary.
Denominal hui-ya preserves the licensed delete-or-retain alternative.
An unbound final ya spelling does not impersonate root-plus-ya structure.
Every liz noun retains its compositional action reading.
Way-of, nature, state, condition, and appearance readings require typed lexical or contextual evidence.
The fixed ca-h matrix remains identity-specific because Canvas makes that lexical relation fixed.
The tla-chiya reading retains its typed participant structure and does not generalize to other liz nouns.
Groups 4 through 6 add no example-stem, visible-letter, translation, formula, or surface authority.
A compound active-action noun preserves the complete owner-issued future verb core and its typed internal boundaries.
The embed, connective or derivational material, matrix, participants, and vowel quantity remain attached to the captured Source analysis.
In huetz-Ø-t-o, t remains a connective and on-o remains the matrix; no t-o verbstem class is created.
Any licensed typed compound Source receives the structural rule without Canvas-example membership.
Intransitive active-action and potential-patient nounstems may be phonologically identical without becoming the same grammatical analysis.
Third-person singular can preserve genuine active-action versus potential-patient ambiguity.
A different person or number can identify the potential-patient analysis.
A transitive active-action noun preserves its nonspecific object while the potential-patient noun lacks that object.
A transitive potential-patient request requires a typed projective-object Source relation rather than a translation guess.
The reflexive-plus-tla exception remains an active-action noun and preserves reflexive ne when tla is absent from the nounstem.
A general-action noun captures the exact owner-issued impersonal future VNC Result.
The impersonal Source may arrive through a nonactive suffix or the separate tla-impersonal operation.
The complete impersonal morphology remains inside the derived liz nounstem.
The general-action target has a nonanimate common subject and names an action performed generally by everyone involved.
The huiloaliztli warning remains spelling guidance and never becomes a grammar control.
Changing the Source shape while preserving valid clause facts does not change eligibility for Groups 7 through 9.
Changing participant, valence, voice, or owner-identity facts while preserving the stem blocks or changes the analysis as required.
Groups 7 through 9 add no compound-stem list, translation authority, formula authority, surface authority, or copied-Result authority.
An action NNC continuation begins with an exact owner-issued active-action NNC Result rather than a nounstem string.
The captured action NNC retains its exact future VNC ancestry, Source analysis, suffix, state, and possessor.
The user chooses the intended licensed matrix and only a genuinely open embed-matrix semantic relation.
Nominal continuation passes the exact action Result to the canonical NNC compound path.
Verbal continuation passes the exact action Result to the canonical VNC compound path.
Copied, JSON-lookalike, formula, surface, and example-identity inputs cannot authorize action-NNC continuation.
At a typed z or liz plus tzin boundary, s-to-tz assimilation applies automatically.
The underlying z or liz and following tzin remain available in the fuller Source analysis.
Conventional spelling and doubled phonetic spelling are reading facts rather than grammar controls.
Active-action and passive-action analyses retain their exact typed VNC voice histories.
In possessive state, the active-action possessor is derived as the agent.
In possessive state, the passive-action possessor is derived as the patient.
The possessor role cannot be manually relabeled independently of typed voice.
Overlapping surface forms or English translations do not merge active and passive analyses.
A Source analysis choice is exposed only where typed grammar and context leave a real ambiguity.
Groups 10 through 12 add no manual assimilation, manual possessor-role, copied-Result, formula, surface, or example authority.
An active-action NNC may serve as a supplementary object only through its exact owner-issued Result.
Lesson 37 reuses the shared supplementation owner and creates no second supplementation engine.
Typed participant roles, referent identity, and acyclicity determine the action-NNC supplementation link.
Changing a valid action Source shape while preserving clause facts preserves supplementation eligibility.
Copied action Results, nounstem identity, formula, and surface similarity cannot authorize supplementation.
Patientives preserve five Source families: passive, impersonal, perfective active, imperfective active, and root or stock.
A typed lō boundary deletes final ō and retains l.
A typed lō-hua boundary deletes ō-hua and retains l.
A typed ō boundary deletes the complete nonactive suffix.
A typed ō-hua boundary deletes the complete extended nonactive suffix.
A typed hua boundary deletes hua and applies the licensed preceding-vowel behavior.
The patientive noun class follows the typed truncation family automatically.
Irregular formation and lexicalized meaning require typed lexical or contextual analysis rather than final-letter guessing.
A passive patientive captures an exact owner-issued passive VNC Result.
The captured passive Result must preserve transitive active ancestry; an intransitive active Source cannot enter this route.
Nonspecific projective and shuntline reflexive evidence remain attached to the passive Source when present.
The no-object passive branch is recorded explicitly when a single specific projective object supplied the passive subject.
A passive history cannot be reconstructed from a patientive surface or a typed-looking raw stem.
Groups 13 through 15 add no stem whitelist, final-letter authority, copied-Result authority, formula authority, surface authority, or manual participant-role control.
An lō passive patientive begins with the exact owner-issued passive VNC Result.
The typed lō boundary deletes final ō and retains l automatically.
Long ī or ō before retained l is preserved.
Preceding a receives the licensed reduced-long pronunciation written without a macron.
The lō patientive receives tli class without a manual class choice.
A narrow lexical or figurative lō reading requires typed Source or contextual evidence.
An ō passive patientive begins with the exact owner-issued passive VNC Result.
The complete typed ō passive suffix is removed automatically.
The active Source, passive layer, participants, and object evidence remain attached after ō truncation.
Human and nonhuman patient referent facts remain distinct from suffix shape.
A spouse, messenger, flour, meal, neck, or other lexical ō reading is not selected by the suffix.
A hua passive patientive begins with the exact owner-issued passive VNC Result.
Deleting typed hua shortens preceding long ī to i in the regular environment.
Deleting hua does not automatically shorten another preceding long vowel such as ō.
Supportive initial-vowel analysis, reduplication, and internal boundaries remain in the captured Source history.
An owner-issued unexpected or irregular nonactive Source remains eligible and does not become a failed route.
Nahuatl patientive construal remains authoritative where English intuition suggests an active reading.
Canvas examples prove the three suffix-family rules but never authorize Source admission.
Groups 16 through 18 add no stem whitelist, final-letter authority, English-meaning authority, copied-Result authority, formula authority, or surface authority.
A reflexive passive patientive inherits shuntline ne automatically from the exact passive transformation.
The active reflexive Source, passive layer, patientive referent, and complete morphemic chain remain attached.
Reflexivity cannot be inserted manually or reconstructed from the final surface.
Promise, vow, and other narrow reflexive-patientive meanings require typed lexical Source or contextual evidence.
A double-object passive patientive keeps exactly the object that survives the owner-issued passive transformation.
The promoted object supplies the patientive referent while the surviving object remains internal to the nounstem.
A surviving nonspecific-human tē exposes the Canvas-licensed retain-or-delete choice productively, without a stem list.
No surviving object other than tē can use that deletion choice.
Participant roles come from typed object and passive frames rather than prefix order or translation.
Groups 19 and 20 add no manual ne control, arbitrary object deletion, example-stem gate, prefix-order authority, copied-Result authority, formula authority, or surface authority.
